mainTopic: אשם תלוי for a doubt of מעילה: the sources of רבי עקיבא and the חכמים, the two-שקלים minimum for every אשם, רבי טרפון's conditional אשם, and the new משנה on doubtful offerings.
overview: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא learns from the ו of ״ואם נפש״ that a person unsure whether he committed מעילה brings an אשם תלוי, and the חכמים exempt him. רב פפא shows that everyone learns an earlier passage from a later one. The חכמים instead rely on a גזירה שוה of ״מצות״ from חטאת, which limits אשם תלוי to sins carrying כרת, and מעילה has no כרת. The גמרא then works through who holds 'no גזירה שוה for half' and 'no היקש for half', and concludes that everyone agrees to both rules. רבי עקיבא learns from ״זאת תורת האשם״ that every אשם must be worth two silver שקלים. The חכמים still need the ו to apply that rule to the אשם תלוי. For a view that does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״, the גמרא supplies the גזירות שוות ״בערכך״ and ״איל״. Next, רבא explains רבי טרפון's conditional אשם in the משנה, and teaches that an אשם ודאי does not need knowledge of the sin in advance. A new משנה follows: a doubtful bird חטאת that becomes definite, and the case of eating one of two pieces of meat, one חולין and one הקדש. רבי יוסי's opinion on that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: does a doubtful case of misuse of holy property bring an אשם תלוי?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the word 'וְאִם' that a person unsure whether he committed מעילה brings an אשם תלוי. The חכמים exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "And if anyone" (the 'and' teaches) that a person is liable to bring an אשם תלוי for an uncertain case of מעילה. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. The חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת: רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי for a doubtful case of מעילה, and the חכמים do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section on אשם תלוי (ויקרא 5:17) starts with 'וְאִם', and that word 'and' comes right after the section on מעילה. רבי עקיבא reads the 'and' as a link: the doubt case of the later section also covers the earlier topic of מעילה. The חכמים do not accept this conclusion, but the ברייתא does not yet say why.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
A doubtful case of misusing הקדש (holy property)
Using הקדש for personal benefit
They exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two offerings. Someone who definitely committed מעילה brings a regular אשם מעילות. The argument here is only about the doubtful case: does he bring an אשם תלוי?

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Rabbis taught: "And if anyone"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17. The word 'and' links this passage to the one right before it, about מעילה.

phrases.aramaic: לְחַיֵּיב עַל סְפֵק מְעִילוֹת אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: to make one liable to bring an אשם תלוי for an uncertain case of misuse,
these are the words of רבי עקיבא; and the Sages exempt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְאִם נֶפֶשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: a doubtful case of מעילה brings an אשם תלוי, learned from the 'ו' of 'וְאִם'. חכמים: he is exempt.

steps.title: Suggestion: do they argue about learning an earlier passage from a later one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the מחלוקת depends on whether we can learn an earlier passage (עליון) from a later passage (תחתון).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about this: רבי עקיבא holds that we learn the earlier passage from the later one, and the Rabbis hold that we do not learn the earlier passage from the later one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a general principle that might explain the argument. This is a proposal, and it sets up the next step, where it gets tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מעילה section is the earlier passage (עליון), and the אשם תלוי section is the later one (תחתון). If you are allowed to learn earlier from later, then the doubt rule of the later section applies to מעילה, which fits רבי עקיבא. If you are not allowed, it does not apply, which fits the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion)
They argue
We learn the earlier passage from the later passage

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'עליון' (upper) and 'תחתון' (lower) are not about height. They mean the earlier and the later passage in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: Shall we say that they argue about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: לְמֵדִין עֶלְיוֹן מִתַּחְתּוֹן,
phrases.english: that רבי עקיבא holds we learn the upper passage from the lower one,
phrases.notes: 'Upper' means the earlier passage, about מעילה. 'Lower' means the later passage, about אשם תלוי.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אֵין לְמֵדִין עֶלְיוֹן מִתַּחְתּוֹן?
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold we do not learn the upper passage from the lower one?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the מחלוקת based on whether an earlier passage can be learned from a later one?

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees we learn earlier from later
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the suggestion. Everyone must agree we learn earlier from later, or there would be no source for slaughtering a bull עולה in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees we learn the earlier passage from the later one. If not, you would not find the rule of slaughtering in the north for a young bull.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back the suggestion of step 2. He shows that the חכמים cannot reject the principle of learning earlier from later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's section on a bull עולה (ויקרא 1:3–9) never says it must be slaughtered in the north (צפון). Only the next section, on a sheep or goat עולה, says 'צפונה' (1:11), and it opens with 'וְאִם'. We all agree a bull עולה needs צפון, so everyone must learn the earlier section from the later one.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
The northern part of the עזרה, where קדשי קדשים are slaughtered
A young bull
You would not find it (no source)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that learning earlier from later is accepted by all, so the מחלוקת needs a different explanation.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees that we learn the upper passage from the lower one,
for if it were so (that we don't),

phrases.aramaic: צָפוֹן בְּבֶן בָּקָר לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לְהוּ,
phrases.english: you would not find (a source for) the north with a young bull,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְמֵדִין עֶלְיוֹן מִתַּחְתּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation suggested in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the חכמים deny learning earlier from later.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Without that principle there would be no source for slaughtering a bull עולה in the north, which is accepted by all.

steps.title: The real reason of the חכמים: a גזירה שוה from חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים exempt because they learn אשם תלוי from חטאת through the shared word 'מצות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here this is the reason the Rabbis exempt: they have a tradition that 'commandments' (here) is learned from 'commandments' (there), from חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first explanation, רב פפא gives the real reason the חכמים exempt a doubtful case of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מצות' appears in the אשם תלוי passage (ויקרא 5:17) and in the חטאת passage (ויקרא 4:27). This גזירה שוה ties אשם תלוי to the same kind of sins as the חטאת. The next steps spell out what that kind of sin is, and why מעילה does not fit: it carries no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
Because they learn it by tradition
A גזירה שוה based on the shared word 'commandments'
A sin offering

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees we learn an earlier passage from a later one. The חכמים exempt a doubtful case of מעילה only because the גזירה שוה of 'מצות' ties אשם תלוי to חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּפָטְרִי:
phrases.english: Rather, here this is the reason of the Rabbis who exempt:
for they learn 'commandments' 'commandments' from the sin offering.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17 and ויקרא 4:27 both use the word 'מצות', so they are linked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּפָטְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation of step 2 with the real reason of the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the חכמים (a גזירה שוה) instead of a general principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים reject learning earlier from later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים accept that principle, but they exempt because of the גזירה שוה 'מצות' from חטאת.

steps.title: What the 'מצות' comparison teaches the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to חטאת limits אשם תלוי to sins whose deliberate version brings כרת and whose accidental version brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there (the regular חטאת), we are talking about a sin that brings כרת if done on purpose, a חטאת if done by accident, and an אשם תלוי if you're unsure. So too here, an אשם תלוי is brought only for that kind of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the חכמים learn from the shared word 'מצות' that was mentioned in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison creates a three-part pattern: on purpose leads to כרת, by accident leads to חטאת, and unsure leads to אשם תלוי. A sin can get an אשם תלוי only if it fits this whole pattern. This sets up the next step, which shows that מעילה does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing a sin on purpose
Doing a sin by accident, without knowing
Being unsure whether you sinned at all
Being 'cut off', a punishment from Heaven
Just as there... so too here. This is how a comparison is set out

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the three levels: זדון (on purpose), שגגה (by accident), and ספק (unsure). Each one has its own result, so don't mix them up.

phrases.english: Just as there, it is a matter
phrases.notes: 'There' means the regular חטאת, where the word 'מצות' also appears.

phrases.english: for which one is liable to כרת if he does it on purpose
and to a חטאת if he does it by accident,
and to an אשם תלוי if he is unsure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת
phrases.english: so too, anything for which one is liable to כרת if done on purpose
and to a חטאת for its uncertain case
phrases.notes: The words 'unsure' and 'by accident' look switched in this line and the next. It means the same as the first half: by accident brings a חטאת, unsure brings an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: and to an אשם תלוי for its accidental case,

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן דָּבָר שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the content of the 'מצות' comparison that step 4 brought.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Spells out the source behind the חכמים's ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשם תלוי comes only for a sin that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by accident.

steps.title: מעילה is left out because it has no כרת
steps.stepSummary: The comparison excludes מעילה, since doing מעילה on purpose does not bring כרת. A ברייתא proves this.
steps.simpleTranslation: This leaves out מעילה, because a person is not punished with כרת for doing it on purpose. As a ברייתא teaches: if someone does מעילה on purpose, רבי says he gets death from Heaven, and the חכמים say it is a regular prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the comparison leaves out מעילה, and brings a ברייתא to prove that מעילה done on purpose never brings כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי and the חכמים argue about the punishment for doing מעילה on purpose. One says death from Heaven, the other says a plain prohibition, but neither one says כרת. Since מעילה fails the כרת test from step 5, the חכמים exempt someone unsure about מעילה from an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave out, to exclude
Using הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit
He did it on purpose
Death, here meaning death from Heaven
A regular Torah prohibition, punished by lashes

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים exempt מעילה from an אשם תלוי because an אשם תלוי needs a sin that brings כרת when done on purpose, and מעילה never does.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, not רבי עקיבא from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: to exclude מעילה,
since one is not liable to כרת for doing it on purpose,
as it is taught: one who did מעילה on purpose –
רבי says: he is liable to death,
phrases.notes: He means death from Heaven, which is not the same as כרת.

phrases.english: and the חכמים say: it is a plain prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מְעִילָה, דְּאֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 5 to leave out מעילה, and proves with a ברייתא that מעילה has no כרת.
steps.raayaObject: That doing מעילה on purpose does not bring כרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי says death from Heaven and the חכמים say a plain prohibition. Neither says כרת.

steps.title: How רבי עקיבא uses the same comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא also learns 'מצות' from חטאת, but only to teach that an אשם תלוי needs a fixed חטאת. That leaves out sins that bring a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds: when we compare 'מצות' to 'מצות' from the חטאת for eating חלב, this is what we learn: just as there it is a fixed חטאת, so too here it must be for a sin that brings a fixed חטאת. This leaves out sins that bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, which do not get an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא answers the חכמים's source. He accepts the comparison, but says it teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides learn from the 'מצות' comparison, so their argument is about what the comparison teaches. For רבי עקיבא, it teaches only that the sin must bring a fixed חטאת. It does not require כרת, so it does not leave out מעילה. That is why his 'וְאִם' source from step 1 can still include מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed חטאת, always the same animal no matter how rich or poor the person is
A 'rising and falling' offering, which changes based on how much money the person has
Forbidden fats, the classic example of a sin that brings a חטאת
We learn it, we derive it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the 'מצות' comparison. The חכמים use it to require כרת, which leaves out מעילה. רבי עקיבא uses it only to require a fixed חטאת, which leaves out קרבן עולה ויורד but keeps מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument is not over whether to use the comparison, but over what it teaches. That explains how רבי עקיבא can make someone unsure about מעילה bring an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא holds:
when we learn 'מצות' from 'מצות'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17 and ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: from the חטאת for eating חלב,
it is for this that we learn it:
just as there it is a fixed offering,
so too here it is for a fixed offering,
to exclude a sliding-scale offering, which does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: כִּי יָלְפִינַן מִצְוֹת מִצְוֹת מֵחַטַּאת חֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers for רבי עקיבא, explaining why the comparison the חכמים used in steps 4 to 6 does not leave out מעילה for him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think that accepting the 'מצות' comparison means agreeing that only sins with כרת bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, the comparison only requires a fixed חטאת. It leaves out קרבן עולה ויורד, not מעילה.

steps.title: The חכמים hold a גזירה שוה cannot work for half
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use the full comparison to חטאת. A גזירה שוה cannot be applied for only half a matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים hold: there is no גזירה שוה for half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חכמים use the full comparison between אשם תלוי and חטאת, while רבי עקיבא uses only part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the word 'מצות' links אשם תלוי to חטאת, the חכמים say you must take the whole comparison. That includes the rule that the sin must carry כרת when done on purpose. So מעילה, which has no כרת, is left out of אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both places.
For half. Using a comparison for only some of its details.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
There is no verbal analogy for half.
phrases.notes: Once you learn from a shared word, you take the whole comparison, not just the parts you like.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אֵין גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the חכמים disagree with רבי עקיבא's partial use of the 'מצות' comparison in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying principle behind the חכמים' view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sides use the same גזירה שוה in the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים apply the full גזירה שוה because a גזירה שוה cannot be used for half.

steps.title: Would רבי עקיבא then hold there is a גזירה שוה for half?
steps.stepSummary: If that is the dispute, רבי עקיבא would hold that a גזירה שוה can work for half. That is a position nobody holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it follow that רבי עקיבא holds there is a גזירה שוה for half?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave, because of what it would mean for רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים disagree with רבי עקיבא because of the rule 'no גזירה שוה for half', then רבי עקיבא must reject that rule. But no one holds that a גזירה שוה can be used for half. So the explanation in step 8 cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference. Something that follows from what was just said.

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Akiva holds:
There is a verbal analogy for half?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 8 by pointing out what it implies about רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dispute is about גזירה שוה למחצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 8 forces רבי עקיבא to hold a position, יש גזירה שוה למחצה, that nobody holds.

steps.title: A new reason for רבי עקיבא: the ו in 'ואם נפש'
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees there is no גזירה שוה for half. רבי עקיבא's real source is the ו of 'ואם נפש'. The ו joins the אשם תלוי passage to the earlier מעילה passage, so the earlier passage learns from the later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees there is no גזירה שוה for half. רבי עקיבא's reason is this: the verse says 'ואם נפש'. The ו adds to the earlier subject, and the earlier passage is learned from the later one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first explanation. It gives רבי עקיבא a different source for requiring an אשם תלוי when someone is unsure whether he did מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The passage about אשם תלוי (ויקרא ה:יז) opens with 'ואם', 'and if'. The 'and' ties it to the passage just before it, which is about מעילה (ויקרא ה:טו-טז). Because of that link, the מעילה passage takes on the rule of the later passage: a doubt brings an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו (and) adds to the subject before it. The two passages are linked.
The upper, earlier passage. Here, מעילה.
The lower, later passage. Here, אשם תלוי.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Earlier learns from later' means the מעילה passage takes a rule from the אשם תלוי passage. It is not the other way around.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
there is no verbal analogy for half,
rather this is Rabbi Akiva's reason,
for the verse says: 'And if anyone'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:יז

phrases.english: the vav adds to the previous matter,
and the upper is learned from the lower.
phrases.notes: The upper passage is מעילה, so a doubt about מעילה also brings an אשם תלוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 9 and replaces step 8 with a new explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether a גזירה שוה can be used for half.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא's source is a היקש from the ו linking the two passages.

steps.title: The חכמים: the link teaches the later passage from the earlier one
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the ו teaches only that the later passage, אשם תלוי, learns from the earlier one. So an אשם תלוי must be worth two silver שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים hold: it is the later passage that learns from the earlier one, teaching that the אשם must be worth silver שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the חכמים read the same ו. They do not accept רבי עקיבא's conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the link goes one way only. The אשם תלוי takes the rule of the מעילה passage: its ram must be worth at least two silver שקלים. The מעילה passage does not take the rule of a doubt from the אשם תלוי passage.

keyTerms.meaning: Silver שקלים. The ram of an אשם must be worth at least two.
Learns, derives.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
it is the lower that learns from the upper
for a guilt offering worth silver shekels.
phrases.notes: From the מעילה passage, ויקרא ה:טו, which says the ram must be worth silver שקלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: תַּחְתּוֹן הוּא דְּגָמַר מֵעֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reading of the same link that רבי עקיבא uses in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the link
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The link would make the earlier passage learn from the later one.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the חכמים, the link only teaches the later passage from the earlier one.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a היקש cannot work for half
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that a היקש cannot be used for only half. If the two passages are linked, the link works both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: there is no היקש for half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי עקיבא's reply to the חכמים' one-way reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ו creates a היקש between the passages, you cannot use only one direction of it. So the מעילה passage must also learn from the אשם תלוי passage, and a doubt of מעילה brings an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two subjects placed together in the תורה. Each learns rules from the other.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
There is no juxtaposition for half.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: אֵין הֶיקֵּשׁ לְמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא's reply to the one-way reading in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the principle that decides the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The link could be used in one direction only, as the חכמים say.
steps.terutzMaskana: A היקש cannot be split, so it works in both directions.

steps.title: Would the חכמים then hold a היקש can work for half?
steps.stepSummary: If that is the dispute, the חכמים would hold that a היקש can work for half. But it is an accepted rule that there is no היקש for half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it follow that the חכמים hold there is a היקש for half? But we hold that there is no היקש for half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 12. The same problem that came up with the גזירה שוה now comes up with the היקש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא's argument rests on 'no היקש for half', then the חכמים must reject that rule. But the rule is accepted by everyone. So the dispute cannot rest on this point. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold it as an established rule.

phrases.english: By inference, the Rabbis hold:
There is a juxtaposition for half?
But we hold as established
that there is no juxtaposition for half!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: יֵשׁ הֶיקֵּשׁ לְמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 12 the same way step 9 attacked step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dispute is about היקש למחצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 12 forces the חכמים to hold יש היקש למחצה, which goes against an established rule.

steps.title: Everyone agrees there is no היקש for half; a separate source removes מעילה
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree there is no היקש for half. The חכמים have a separate גזירה שוה, ״מצות״ ״מצות״, that takes מעילה out of the היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees there is no היקש for half. Here, the reason of the חכמים is that they have a גזירה שוה of 'commandments' 'commandments', and that takes this case out of the היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 13. The חכמים do not hold that a היקש works for half. A different source removes one part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש made by the ו would normally work both ways. The חכמים have an outside source, a גזירה שוה from חטאת using the word ״מצות״, that limits אשם תלוי to the kind of sins that need a חטאת. That outside source cancels the part of the היקש that would bring an אשם תלוי for a doubt of מעילה, so the היקש itself is not split in half.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two passages that works only halfway or in one direction. Everyone rejects this.
'For they learn it'. This points to a learned source, here a גזירה שוה.
The word 'commandments' appears in both the אשם תלוי passage and the חטאת passage. That shared word links them.
'It took it out of the היקש'. Another source overrides part of the comparison.

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying the היקש itself works one way only. The היקש is whole, but a separate גזירה שוה blocks one of its results.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees there is no comparison of passages for half,
and here, this is the reason of the Rabbis:
for they learn from "commandments" and "commandments",
phrases.notes: The word appears in ויקרא 5:17 (אשם תלוי) and ויקרא 4:27 (חטאת).

phrases.english: and that took it out of the comparison.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין הֶיקֵּשׁ לְמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13 that the חכמים would be holding there is a היקש for half.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An outside source overrides part of the היקש, so no split היקש is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to be using the היקש in only one direction.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone holds there is no היקש for half. The חכמים have a גזירה שוה that removes מעילה from the היקש.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source for the two-שקלים rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns that every אשם, including אשם תלוי, must be worth two silver שקלים from ״זאת תורת האשם״, which means there is one law for all אשמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא learns that an אשם must be worth silver שקלים from 'This is the law of the guilt offering', meaning there is one law for all guilt offerings, so every אשם must be worth silver שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי עקיבא gets the rule that an אשם תלוי must be worth two silver שקלים. He does not need the ו for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the ו is the source that an אשם תלוי must be worth two שקלים. רבי עקיבא gets that rule from ״זאת תורת האשם״ instead. That frees the ו to teach the other direction: the earlier passage learns from the later one, so a doubt of מעילה brings an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Silver שקלים. An אשם must be worth at least two silver שקלים.
'This is the law of the guilt offering' (ויקרא 7:1).
'One law for all guilt offerings'. All types of אשם share the same rules.
'He derives it from'. This introduces someone's source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
that a guilt offering must be worth silver shekels,
he derives from "This is the law of the guilt offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:1

phrases.english: there is one law for all the guilt offerings,
teaching that a guilt offering must be worth silver shekels.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אָשָׁם בְּכֶסֶף שְׁקָלִים נָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the חכמים, the גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא gets the two-שקלים rule without the ו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives an alternate source, which frees the ו for a different teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא learns the two-שקלים rule for all אשמות from ״זאת תורת האשם״.

steps.title: Why the חכמים still need ״ואם נפש״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים do not use ״זאת תורת האשם״. It answers that the ו of ״ואם נפש״ was still needed to teach that the later passage learns from the earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? Even though it says 'This is the law of the guilt offering', the תורה still needed to write 'And if a person'. The ו adds onto the earlier topic, so the later passage learns from the earlier one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if ״זאת תורת האשם״ already teaches the two-שקלים rule, why do the חכמים need the ו? It answers that the ו was still necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the ו so that the אשם תלוי passage learns from the earlier מעילה passage, which means the אשם תלוי must be worth two שקלים. The גמרא says this teaching was needed even with ״זאת תורת האשם״ in the תורה. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if a person' (ויקרא 5:17). This opens the אשם תלוי passage.
'A ו adds onto the earlier topic'. It joins the new passage to the one before it.
'The lower is learned from the upper'. The later passage takes rules from the earlier one.
'It was needed'. The extra verse is shown to be necessary.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The question is: why don't the Rabbis just use ״זאת תורת האשם״ like רבי עקיבא does?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִיב ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם״,
phrases.english: Even though it is written "This is the law of the guilt offering,"
it was necessary to write "And if a person":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17

phrases.english: the letter vav adds onto the earlier topic,
and the lower passage is learned from the upper one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן? אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִיב ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the obvious follow-up to Step 15: why don't the חכמים rely on the same verse?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that an apparently extra source is necessary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״זאת תורת האשם״ should be enough, so the ו would not be needed for the two-שקלים rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו is still needed so that the later passage, אשם תלוי, learns from the earlier one.

steps.title: ״זאת תורת האשם״ alone would cover only definite אשמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why the ו is needed. From ״זאת תורת האשם״ alone, one would say the rule of one law for all אשמות applies only to the other definite אשמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had 'This is the law of the guilt offering', I would have said: when I say there is one law for all guilt offerings, that applies only to the other definite guilt offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts giving the reason the חכמים need the ו. The sentence finishes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת תורת האשם״ makes all אשמות equal, but someone could limit that to an אשם brought for a sin we know happened (an אשם ודאי). An אשם תלוי is brought only for a doubt, so it might have been left out. The ו is needed to include it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I would have thought'. This is a mistaken first assumption.
'These words apply only to...'. It limits a rule.
Definite guilt offerings: אשמות brought when the sin is known for sure, unlike an אשם תלוי.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a הוה אמינא, a mistaken first thought, and the sentence is not finished yet. The גמרא is explaining what we might have wrongly concluded without the ו.

phrases.english: And if it were only from "This is the law of the guilt offering,"
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמֵינָא תּוֹרָה אַחַת לְכׇל אֲשָׁמוֹת –
phrases.english: when I say there is one law for all guilt offerings,
that applies only to other definite guilt offerings,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִ״זֹּאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the reasoning behind Step 16's claim that the ו was necessary.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A הוה אמינא that shows the general verse has limited scope.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״זאת תורת האשם״ would apply only to definite אשמות, not to an אשם תלוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: So the ו of ״ואם נפש״ is needed to apply the two-שקלים rule to an אשם תלוי. Step 18 finishes the explanation.

steps.title: Without the ו, an אשם תלוי might be as cheap as a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: An אשם תלוי comes for a doubt about eating חלב, and the definite case of חלב needs only a cheap חטאת. So one might think the doubtful case could also be cheap. The ו of ״ואם נפש״ teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an אשם תלוי comes for a doubt about eating forbidden fat. So I might say: the doubt should not be stricter than the definite sin. Just as the definite sin needs only a חטאת worth a tiny coin, the doubt should need only an אשם worth a tiny coin. That is why the Torah wrote ״ואם נפש״ with a ו, which adds on to the earlier topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the point it started in step 17. It explains why ״זאת תורת האשם״ alone would not be enough to require two silver שקלים for an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is tied to a sin, like eating חלב, whose definite version needs only a חטאת of any value. That gives a strong reason to think the doubtful offering could also be cheap. The ו links the אשם תלוי passage to the earlier מעילה passage, which requires two silver שקלים, and so it blocks that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'suspended' guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he did a sin
A doubt whether one ate forbidden fat
The doubtful case should not be stricter than the definite case
A small coin, one-sixth of a dinar
The letter ו adds on to the earlier topic and links the two passages

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the חכמים use the ו for this purpose instead of using it to bring an אשם תלוי for a doubt about מעילה, as רבי עקיבא does.

phrases.english: But a provisional guilt offering,
since it comes for a doubt about forbidden fat,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: לָא יְהֵא סְפֵיקוֹ חָמוּר מִוַּדָּאוֹ,
phrases.english: I might say: its doubtful case should not be stricter than its definite case,
just as its definite case is a sin offering worth a danka,
phrases.notes: A דנקא is a tiny coin, one-sixth of a דינר. A חטאת has no minimum price.

phrases.english: so too its doubtful case would be a guilt offering worth a danka.
For this reason the Merciful One wrote: "And if a person":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:17, the opening of the אשם תלוי passage.

phrases.english: the vav adds on to the earlier topic.
phrases.notes: The earlier topic is the מעילה passage, where the אשם must be worth two silver שקלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, כֵּיוָן דְּעַל סְפֵק חֵלֶב קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun in step 17 of why the ו is needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the verse is needed for a separate purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An אשם תלוי, coming for a doubt about חלב, could be worth as little as a דנקא, like the חטאת for the definite sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו links the אשם תלוי to the מעילה passage, so it too must be worth two silver שקלים.

steps.title: For one who does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״, where does the two-שקלים rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: Requiring the same minimum value for all אשמות works for anyone who expounds ״זאת תורת האשם״. But what does someone who does not expound that verse say?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who learns from ״זאת תורת האשם״. But for the one who does not learn from ״זאת תורת האשם״, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a view that does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״ at all. Where does that view learn that the other definite אשמות must be worth two silver שקלים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא (step 15) and the חכמים (step 16) both use ״זאת תורת האשם״ to give the definite אשמות one law. But some hold that this verse is not expounded at all. That view still needs a source for the other definite אשמות, like אשם גזילות.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well
According to the one who expounds (a verse)
What can be said? (a challenge asking for a source or answer)

phrases.english: It works out well for the one who expounds "This is the law of the guilt offering,"
phrases.notes: Both רבי עקיבא (step 15) and the חכמים (step 16) learn from this verse.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם״,
phrases.english: but for the one who does not expound "This is the law of the guilt offering,"
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיחָא לְמַאן דְּדָרֵישׁ ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם״, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained the sources of רבי עקיבא and the חכמים, the גמרא asks about a view that does not use ״זאת תורת האשם״ at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without that verse, there seems to be no source that every definite אשם must be worth two silver שקלים.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from ״בערכך״
steps.stepSummary: The view that does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״ learns the two-שקלים rule for the other אשמות from the word ״בערכך״, which also appears by אשם מעילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from ״בערכך״ ״בערכך״, comparing to the אשם of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this view uses a גזירה שוה. The word ״בערכך״ appears both by אשם מעילות and by the other אשמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מעילה, ״בערכך כסף שקלים״ clearly means two silver שקלים. Since the same word ״בערכך״ appears by the other definite אשמות, the same minimum applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from one place to another because the same word appears in both
"By your valuation": the Torah's word for the set value of the אשם
The guilt offering brought for misusing הקדש property

phrases.english: He derives it from "by your valuation" and "by your valuation"
phrases.notes: The word appears by מעילה (ויקרא 5:15) and by the other אשמות (ויקרא 5:18, 5:25).

phrases.english: from the guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלֵיף ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ מֵאֲשַׁם מְעִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״זאת תורת האשם״, this view would have no source for the minimum value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה of ״בערכך״ gives the other אשמות the two-שקלים minimum of אשם מעילות.

steps.title: The אשם of שפחה חרופה does not say ״בערכך״
steps.stepSummary: The ״בערכך״ גזירה שוה cannot cover the אשם of שפחה חרופה, because ״בערכך״ is not written there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אשם for a שפחה חרופה does not have ״בערכך״ written by it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 20. One אשם, the אשם of שפחה חרופה, does not use the word ״בערכך״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה needs the same word in both places. Since that אשם passage does not say ״בערכך״, the view that does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״ still lacks a source for its minimum value.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering for relations with a maidservant who is designated (betrothed) to a Jewish man

phrases.english: The guilt offering for an espoused maidservant,
"by your valuation" is not written about it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשַׁם שִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה, לָא כְּתִב בֵּהּ ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the ״בערכך״ גזירה שוה from step 20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״בערכך״ is missing from the שפחה חרופה passage, so the גזירה שוה cannot apply there.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from ״איל״
steps.stepSummary: For the אשם of שפחה חרופה, we learn from the word ״איל״ (ram), which appears there and by אשם מעילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from ״איל״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a different גזירה שוה. Both the מעילה passage and the שפחה חרופה passage use the word ״איל״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שפחה חרופה passage lacks ״בערכך״, but it shares the word ״איל״ with the מעילה passage. So its אשם also needs the two-שקלים minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: A ram, the animal used for these guilt offerings
We derive

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns the two-שקלים rule for all אשמות from ״זאת תורת האשם״. The חכמים use that verse for the definite אשמות and the ו of ״ואם נפש״ for the אשם תלוי. A view that does not expound ״זאת תורת האשם״ uses ״בערכך״ for the other definite אשמות and ״איל״ for the אשם of שפחה חרופה.

phrases.english: We derive it from "ram"
phrases.notes: ״איל״ appears by מעילה (ויקרא 5:15) and by שפחה חרופה (ויקרא 19:21).

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלְפִינַן בְּ״אֵיל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״בערכך״, the אשם of שפחה חרופה would have no minimum value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה of ״איל״ links it to אשם מעילות, so it also needs two silver שקלים.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבי עקיבא concedes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where רבי עקיבא concedes, ending with the words ״ואם ספק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״רבי עקיבא concedes, etc.,״ up to ״and if it is a doubt.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new part of the משנה. It quotes the opening and closing words to set up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line opens a new section. In the משנה, רבי עקיבא concedes that the payment for מעילה is not brought until the sin is known for sure. רבי טרפון says one may bring everything and declare: if it is a doubt, the money is a donation and the אשם is an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Concedes, agrees on this point
Etc. (the rest of the quote is skipped)
And if it is a doubt

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva concedes, etc.
And if it is uncertain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion closes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא concedes that the payment for מעילה waits until the sin is known. רבי טרפון allows bringing it with a conditional declaration covering the doubtful case.

steps.title: What is רבי טרפון saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'ואם ספק' in רבי טרפון's statement mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops on the words just quoted from רבי טרפון and asks what they mean. This question sets up רבא's reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון tells the person to say 'if it is uncertain, the animal is an אשם תלוי.' But the person is already in doubt when he brings it, so the phrase 'if it is uncertain' seems to make no sense. The גמרא wants to know what the stated condition actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? A request to explain a confusing statement

phrases.english: What is he saying?
phrases.notes: This is about רבי טרפון's words 'ואם ספק', the end of the משנה quoted in the previous step.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the end of the משנה line quoted in step 23 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What condition רבי טרפון means by 'if it is uncertain', when the person is already uncertain.

steps.title: רבא rereads the condition as 'if the doubt lasts forever'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says to read it: if the doubt stays forever, the animal is an אשם תלוי, because the same kind of animal is brought for a known sin and for an unknown one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Teach it this way: If his doubt stays forever, let it be an אשם תלוי. This works because the same kind of animal he brings when the sin is known, he brings when it is not known.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by changing how we read the משנה. The condition is not 'if I am uncertain' but 'if my doubt is never cleared up.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the condition makes sense: if he never finds out, the animal stays an אשם תלוי, and if he finds out he sinned, it counts as the real אשם. This is allowed because an אשם תלוי and an אשם מעילות are the same kind of animal, so one animal can serve as either.

keyTerms.meaning: Provisional guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
Known; the case where the person knows he sinned

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'שממין שהוא מביא על הודע מביא על לא הודע' is the basis for one animal working for either case, and the next משנה uses the same rule.

phrases.english: Rava said: Teach it this way:
If his doubt remains forever,
let it be a provisional guilt offering,
since from the same kind he brings for a known sin,
he brings it for a sin that is not known.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, תְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 by rereading the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The condition means 'if the doubt is never resolved, it is an אשם תלוי'; this works because both offerings are the same kind of animal.

steps.title: Once he finds out, shouldn't he need a new אשם ודאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in the end, when the sin becomes known to him, he should have to bring a real אשם ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when it becomes known to him, he needs to bring a definite guilt offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי טרפון's plan. Even with one animal, when he later learns he sinned, it seems he must bring a new אשם ודאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he brought the animal, he did not know he had sinned. The challenge assumes an אשם ודאי only counts if he knew about the sin before bringing it. If so, the animal he already brought cannot be his אשם ודאי, and רבי טרפון's plan to save a second אשם fails.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; no matter what
Definite guilt offering, brought when one knows he sinned
Becomes known

phrases.english: In the end, when it becomes known to him,
he needs to bring a definite guilt offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי טרפון's one-animal plan as explained by רבא in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's plan that one animal serves as the אשם ודאי if he later learns he sinned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an אשם ודאי needs knowledge of the sin before it is brought, an animal brought while he was in doubt cannot count, so a new one is required.

steps.title: An אשם ודאי does not need knowledge in advance
steps.stepSummary: רבא says: we learn from both תנאים that an אשם ודאי does not need the sin to be known from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From the words of both of them we learn: a definite guilt offering does not need knowledge of the sin from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He shows that both רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון hold that an אשם ודאי works even if he only learned about the sin later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge rested on the idea that an אשם ודאי needs knowledge of the sin before it is brought. רבא says both תנאים reject that idea, so finding out later is enough. That means the animal he already brought can count as his אשם ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of both of them we learn
Knowledge that one sinned
From the start; before the act

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם ודאי does not need knowledge of the sin before it is brought. So one animal, brought with a condition, can work as an אשם תלוי or as an אשם ודאי.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying knowledge is never needed. He is saying it does not need to come first; finding out later is enough.

phrases.english: Rava said: From the words of both of them we learn:
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון from the משנה.

phrases.english: a definite guilt offering does not need
knowledge from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִדִּבְרֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם נִלְמַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26 by denying its assumption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge's underlying assumption about what an אשם ודאי requires.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An אשם ודאי only counts if he knew of the sin before bringing it, so a new one is needed after he finds out.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both תנאים hold that knowing of the sin beforehand is not required, so the animal already brought counts.

steps.title: משנה: a doubtful bird חטאת that becomes definite
steps.stepSummary: A woman who brought a bird חטאת out of doubt and learned before the מליקה that she surely gave birth should make it a definite חטאת, because the same kind of bird is brought in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who brought a bird sin offering, and before it was pinched she found out that she surely gave birth, should make it a definite sin offering. This works because the same kind she brings when it is known, she brings when it is not known.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives another case where the offering for a doubt and the offering for a certain sin are the same kind, so one bird can switch to the definite offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman unsure whether her miscarriage obligates a חטאת brings a bird חטאת out of doubt. If she learns before the מליקה that she really gave birth, she does not need a new bird. She makes this one a definite חטאת, for the same reason רבי טרפון gave about the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה
A bird sin offering
Was pinched; the מליקה, the way a bird offering is killed
She should make it a definite offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה uses the same rule as רבי טרפון, 'שממין שהוא מביא על הודע מביא על לא הודע', in a new case.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman who brought a bird sin offering,
before it was pinched,
it became known to her that she surely gave birth,
she should make it a definite offering,
since from the same kind she brings for a known case,
she brings for a case that is not known.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהֵבִיאָה חַטַּאת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that uses the same 'same kind of offering' rule seen in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If, before the מליקה, it becomes known that she surely gave birth, the doubtful bird חטאת is made into a definite חטאת, because the same kind of bird is brought for known and unknown cases.

steps.title: One person ate one of two pieces, then the second
steps.stepSummary: If a person ate one of two pieces (one חולין, one הקדש) and does not know which, the תנא קמא exempts him and רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי. If he then eats the second piece, he brings an אשם ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a piece of plain meat and a piece of holy meat. Someone ate one of them and does not know which one he ate. He is exempt. רבי עקיבא says he must bring an אשם תלוי. If he then ate the second piece too, he brings a definite אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The same משנה continues with a new case. It gives a doubt about eating holy meat, and then shows what happens once the doubt turns into certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one piece eaten, there is a 50/50 doubt whether he used holy property (מעילה). The תנא קמא exempts him, and רבי עקיבא makes him bring an אשם תלוי, matching his view in the earlier משנה that an אשם תלוי is brought even for a doubt of מעילה. Once he eats both pieces, he has certainly eaten the holy one, so everyone agrees he brings an אשם ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece (of meat)
Plain, non-holy food
Holy property that belongs to the בית המקדש
Exempt; he does not have to bring the offering
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
A definite guilt offering, brought when the sin is certain

steps.confusionAlert: In this first case 'פטור' means he does not bring an אשם תלוי, since the תנא קמא holds that no אשם תלוי is brought for a doubt of מעילה. It does not mean the case is unimportant. Once he eats both pieces, everyone agrees he must bring a full אשם ודאי.

phrases.aramaic: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל חוּלִּין וַחֲתִיכָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: A piece of non-sacred meat and a piece of sacred meat,
he ate one of them
and does not know which of them he ate –
he is exempt,
Rabbi Akiva obligates a provisional guilt offering.
If he ate the second one –
he brings a definite guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל חוּלִּין וַחֲתִיכָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה begun in step 28, returning to אשם תלוי for a doubt of מעילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a doubt of eating הקדש, the תנא קמא exempts and רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי. Once both pieces are eaten, the person brings an אשם ודאי.

steps.title: Two people each ate one piece: רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: If one person ate the first piece and someone else ate the second, רבי עקיבא says each one brings his own אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one person ate the first piece and another person came and ate the second piece, each of them brings an אשם תלוי. This is the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case: the two pieces were eaten by two different people. רבי עקיבא gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we know for sure that someone ate the holy meat, but each person on his own is still in doubt. So רבי עקיבא treats each one separately, and each brings an אשם תלוי. Neither can bring an אשם ודאי, because neither knows that he himself sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (piece)
The second (piece)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 29. There, one person ate both pieces, so his sin was certain. Here each person ate only one piece, so each is still unsure about himself.

phrases.english: One person ate the first piece
and another came and ate the second –
this one brings a provisional guilt offering
and that one brings a provisional guilt offering,
the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל אֶחָד אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וּבָא אַחֵר וְאָכַל אֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from one person eating both pieces to two people each eating one piece.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, when two people each ate one piece, each brings his own אשם תלוי.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: both bring one offering together, and רבי יוסי begins
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי עקיבא and says the two people together bring one אשם. Then the משנה starts to bring רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the two of them bring one אשם together. רבי יוסי says:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different ruling for the two-people case. The last words open רבי יוסי's opinion, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's point is that we know for sure one of the two ate the holy meat. So instead of two doubtful offerings, the two can join together and bring one offering, which counts as an אשם ודאי for the one who really sinned. The words 'רבי יוסי אומר' only set up a third opinion, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them
One guilt offering, brought together as partners

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on the two-people case: רבי עקיבא says each brings an אשם תלוי. רבי שמעון says they join and bring one אשם. רבי יוסי's view comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Both of them bring one guilt offering.
Rabbi Yosei says:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶן מְבִיאִין אָשָׁם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different ruling from רבי עקיבא's in step 30 for the same two-people case, then opens רבי יוסי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the two people bring one shared אשם, because one of them surely sinned.
